what_its_for: Perampanel is a seizure medicine (anticonvulsant) used to help control certain types of seizures in people 4 years of age and older. It is used for partial-onset seizures (seizures that start in one part of the brain) and for primary generalized tonic-clonic seizures (grand mal seizures that affect the whole brain). It works by blocking certain signals in the brain that can trigger seizures.
how_to_take: Take perampanel by mouth exactly as your doctor prescribed. It comes as a tablet or an oral liquid suspension. Take it once a day at bedtime, since it can cause dizziness and sleepiness. You can take it with or without food, but try to take it the same way each time. Shake the oral liquid well before each use and use the measuring device that comes with it — never use a kitchen spoon. Swallow tablets whole with a full glass of water.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a low dose and slowly increase it over several weeks to find the right dose for you. The usual starting dose for adults and children 12 and older is 2 mg once a day at bedtime. The dose may be increased by 2 mg every week or every two weeks. The typical maintenance dose ranges from 8 mg to 12 mg per day, but your doctor will decide the best dose for you. Children ages 4 to 11 who weigh less than 66 pounds (30 kg) usually start at 1 mg once daily. Never change your dose or stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first, as stopping suddenly can cause more seizures.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still that same night before you go to sleep. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time the following night. Never take two doses on the same day to make up for a missed one. If you miss doses for 2 weeks or more in a row, call your doctor before restarting, as your dose may need to be adjusted.
storage: Store perampanel tablets and oral suspension at room temperature between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store in the bathroom. Keep the bottle tightly closed. The oral suspension does not need to be refrigerated. Throw away any unused oral suspension 90 days after first opening the bottle. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not flush medicines down the toilet — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of unused medicine.
what_to_avoid: Avoid drinking alcohol while taking perampanel. Alcohol can dangerously increase dizziness, sleepiness, and serious behavior changes such as aggression or irritability. Do not drive, operate heavy machinery, or do activities that require you to be fully alert until you know how this medicine affects you — it can cause significant dizziness and sleepiness, especially when you first start it or when your dose is increased. Avoid taking other medicines that cause sleepiness (such as sleep aids, anxiety medicines, opioid pain medicines, or muscle relaxers) unless your doctor approves. Some medicines can affect how perampanel works, so tell all your doctors and your pharmacist about every medicine, vitamin, and herbal supplement you take.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you or a caregiver notices: new or worsening aggressive behavior, anger, hostility, irritability, or thoughts of harming yourself or others; new or worsening depression or anxiety; thoughts of suicide or self-harm; unusual changes in mood or behavior; severe dizziness or falls; severe skin reaction such as rash, blisters, or peeling skin; or seizures that are getting worse or happening more often. Perampanel has a serious risk of causing psychiatric and behavioral side effects, so it is important to contact your doctor immediately if any mental or mood changes occur.
when_it_works: Perampanel starts working in your body fairly quickly, but it may take several weeks to months before your seizures are fully controlled. Your doctor will gradually increase your dose to find the best level for you. Do not get discouraged if you do not see immediate results. It is very important to take it every day as prescribed, even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it on your own, even if your seizures have stopped.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or plan to become pregnant. Perampanel may harm an unborn baby. Women who can become pregnant should use effective birth control while taking this medicine. Note that perampanel can make some hormonal birth control pills less effective — talk to your doctor about reliable contraception options. Breastfeeding: It is not known if perampanel passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Older adults: Older adults may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and falls, so extra caution is needed. Children: Safety and dosing information is available for children 4 years of age and older. Kidney or liver disease: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, as your dose may need to be adjusted. People with severe liver disease should not use this medicine.
